title: csa-gap-mapping
description: A CSA gap mapping: a standard STIX relationship asserting how much of the source's requirement the target covers, using CSA's gap vocabulary. Read left to right — source_ref is what is mapped FROM. The custom properties are declared by a toplevel-property-extension so they are scoped rather than colliding with other producers' properties on the standard relationship type.
$comment: gap_level is required because a gap mapping without a verdict asserts nothing — it is the substance of the claim, not an annotation on it.

source_ref.description: What is mapped FROM. A catalog control or regulation clause.

target_ref.description: What is mapped TO. A→B and B→A are two separate objects.

gap_level.description: CSA's coverage verdict for this direction. No Gap: the target covers the source's requirement. Partial Gap: partial coverage. Full Gap: the target does not cover it. These are the three values used across CSA's published mappings.

bidirectional.description: True when the relation is symmetric, so the same verdict holds in both directions. STIX relationships are inherently directional, so this is an explicit assertion; a consumer that ignores it still reads the object correctly as source to target, just incompletely.

description.description: Rationale for the mapping — the addendum text in CSA's published mappings, which carries scope qualification and caveats.
